summary: Two passages of Strabo: his report that Posidonius used Plato's Atlantis as an example of land that sinks, and his account of Helike, the Greek city swallowed by the sea in 373 BCE.

tree.title: Strabo, Geography 2.3.6: Posidonius on earthquakes, Plato's Atlantis and the Cimbrians
tree.summary: Strabo says Posidonius rightly notes that land rises and settles, and cites Plato that the Atlantis story may not be a fiction. Posidonius prefers that to saying the inventor "made it disappear" like Homer's Achaean wall. Strabo also reports his idea that a sudden flood drove the Cimbrians out.

tree.title: Strabo, Geography 8.7.2: the sea swallows Helike
tree.summary: Strabo reports that an earthquake lifted the sea and submerged Helike and the temple of Poseidon, two years before Leuctra. Eratosthenes saw the site, ferrymen showed a bronze Poseidon in the strait, and Heracleides gives the Achaean version of Poseidon's anger.
